## Goal:

To produce a figure that allows us to visualize the location and binding of our primers in a reproducable way.

## Packages

```{r}

#| echo: true
#| eval: true

library(tidyverse)
library(Biostrings)

```

## An example with flu and a matrix gene:

Context: This is segment 7 from a HPAI virus that was isolated on Nantucket Island from a Dying GBBG. It was sequenced by Mt. Sinai and below is the sequence from that gene.

We will be using the Biostrings package to visualize it briefly and find the matches for the primers.

```{r}

mgene <- DNAString("")

mgene

```

As we can see it is 1027 bases long and it is important to remember that the orientation of this cDNA is 5' to 3' as is standard in Bioinformatics.

### Load your primers:

Let's also read in our primers which are again written in the 5' to 3' direction.

```{r}
forward <- DNAString("AGATGAGTCTTCTAACCGAGGTCG")
reverse <- DNAString("TGCAAAAACATCTTCAAGTCTCTG")
```

### FInding the matches:

Ok so we want to know where these sequences match to our genome segment. Lets start with the forward primer.

```{r}
forward_match <- matchPattern(pattern = forward,subject = mgene)
print(forward_match)
```

Great so we can see that the match is only in one spot and it starts from position 24 and ends at position 47 of our sequence. It is important to remember the following rules for primer binding in PCR.

-   The forward primer is designed to bind to the complementary 3' to 5' template strand. This is why we can directly search for the pattern in the original sequence because it will match identically so it can bind to the complement.

-   The reverse primer needs to bind to our 'top' or 'original' strand but needs to bind in the 3' to 5' direction. This poses some challenges:

    -   You can't search for it directly since the pattern won't be found.
    -   Our primer is in the 5' to 3' direction not 3' to 5'

We can overcome this by creating the reverse complement of our primer and then searching for it on our sequence.

```{r}

reverse_complement <- reverseComplement(reverse)

reverse_match <- matchPattern(pattern = reverse_complement, subject = mgene,max.mismatch = 1)
print(reverse_match)

```

Amazing! We can find the primer! **Note** I allowed for one mismatch in this primer since I know that at one position there is a mismatch. (This took me longer than I would like to admit to find out)

## Plotting it!

Ok now we want to design a plot for this.

First we need to trim down our M-gene to only the parts that matter for visualization, i.e. the parts between the primers!

```{r}

focal_segment <- mgene[20:125] # I gave some wiggle room on either side for visualization

```

Let's make a empty box that is the same size as our focal segment and then visuzalize it.

```{r}

focal_segment <- as.character(focal_segment)

# Create a blank plot
plot(x=1, 
     type = "n", 
     xlab = "", 
     ylab = "", 
     xlim = c(0, nchar(focal_segment)), 
     ylim = c(0, 1), 
     xaxt = "n", 
     yaxt = "n")

```

Ok now let's add in the letters for our strand 1

```{r}

plot(x=1, 
     type = "n", 
     xlab = "", 
     ylab = "", 
     xlim = c(0, nchar(focal_segment)), 
     ylim = c(0, 1), 
     xaxt = "n", 
     yaxt = "n")

text(x = 1:nchar(focal_segment), 
     y = rep(1, nchar(focal_segment)), 
     labels = strsplit(focal_segment, "")[[1]], 
     cex = 1)

```

Great now let's add the complement of this strand at the bottom

```{r}
comp <- complement(DNAString(focal_segment))

comp <- as.character(comp)

     ylab = "",

     yaxt = "n")

text(x = 1:nchar(focal_segment), 
     y = rep(1, nchar(focal_segment)), 
     labels = strsplit(focal_segment, "")[[1]], 
     cex = 1)

text(x = 1:nchar(comp), 
     y = rep(0.9, nchar(comp)), 
     labels = strsplit(comp, "")[[1]], 
     cex = 1)
```


Alrighty! That's not bad! I would like to roll this into a function to make sure that it is really generalizable eventually.

### Get_primer_matches function:

```{r}

# Going from sequence to matches

primer1 <- DNAString("AGATGAGTCTTCTAACCGAGGTCG")
primer2 <- DNAString("TGCAAAAACATCTTCAAGTCTCTG")
target <- DNAString("")

get_primer_matches <- function(target=target,forward=primer1,reverse=primer2,max.miss=5){
  
# Convert the strings to DNAStrings()
  
target <- DNAString(target)
forward <- DNAString(forward)
reverse <- DNAString(reverse)

#get the max mismatch value
max.miss=max.miss

# find the primer 1 matches:  
p1_match <- Biostrings::matchPattern(pattern = forward,subject = target,max.mismatch = max.miss)
# test if the match length is 0
if (length(p1_match@ranges@width)==0){
  # primer1
  rcomp_primer1 <- reverseComplement(forward)
  rcomp_primer1
  best_match_p1 <- p1_match
  
#   print("The forward primer needed to be reverse complemented to be found in your target")
# p1_rcomp_match <- Biostrings::matchPattern(pattern = reverseComplement((forward)),subject = target,max.mismatch = max.miss)
# print(p1_rcomp_match)
# print(rcomp_primer1)
  print("The forward primer was not found in your sequence. Check to make sure the primer matches or adjust the max.miss value")
} else {
  # if the match is not 0 then report the match
  print("The forward primer matches as is see below....")
  print(p1_match)
  best_match_p1 <- p1_match
}


# find the primer 2 matches
p2_match <- Biostrings::matchPattern(pattern = reverse,subject = target,max.mismatch = max.miss)

# check if the match is there
if (length(p2_match@ranges@width)==0){
  # primer2
  rcomp_primer2 <- reverseComplement(reverse)
  rcomp_primer2
  print("The reverse primer needed to be reverse complemented to be found in your target")
p2_rcomp_match <- Biostrings::matchPattern(pattern = reverseComplement((reverse)),subject = target,max.mismatch = max.miss)
print(p2_rcomp_match)
best_match_p2 <- p2_rcomp_match
} else {
  print("The reverse primer matches as is see below....")
  print(p2_match)
  best_match_p2 <- p2_match
}
# Return the matches in a list
  return(list(p1_match = best_match_p1, p2_match = best_match_p2))
}



```

Let's test our the function:

```{r}
get_primer_matches(target = target,forward = primer1,reverse = primer2,max.miss = 1)
```

Ok let's take a different approach let's make it relative to each DNA strand

```{r}

cox1 |> length()/5
# let's try 300 bp at a time. 

par(mar=c(0,0,1,0))

     type = "n", 
     xlab = "", 
     ylab = "", 
     xlim = c(0,300), 
     ylim = c(0, 1), 
     xaxt = "n",

# Define the range and step size
start_val <- 1
end_val <- 1551
step_size <- 300

# Generate the starting values for each set
start_points <- seq(start_val, end_val, by = step_size)

# Loop through the sets
for (start in start_points) {
  # Calculate the end value for the current set
  end <- min(start + step_size - 1, end_val) # Ensure it doesn't exceed end_val

  # Create the sequence for the current set
  current_set <- start:end

  # Print or process the current set
  cat("Set from", start, "to", end, ":\n")
  print(current_set)
  cat("\n") # Add a newline for better readability
  # You can replace the print(current_set) with whatever operation you need to perform on the current set.
}

```

```{r}
  for (start in start_points) {
    line_num <- which(start_points==start)
  # Calculate the end value for the current set
  end <- min(start + step_size - 1, end_val) # Ensure it doesn't exceed end_val

  # Create the sequence for the current set
    current_set <- start:end

    # get length of section

    # Calculate min and max within the loop
    min_data <- min(current_set) # Use the whole current set
    max_data <- max(current_set) # Use the whole current set
    
    # line number
    line_num <- 
  new_x <- (current_set - min_data) / (max_data - min_data) * 300 # assuming xlim is 0 to 300
  points(x = new_x,y=rep(num_lines[line_num],length(current_set)),cex=1)
  }
  

}
```

```{r}
plot_sequence_full <- function(gap_size=20,seq1,seq2,xlim=100){
par(mar=c(1,1,1,1))
plot(x=1, 
     type = "n", 
     xlab = "", 
     ylab = "", 
     xlim = c(0,xlim), 
     ylim = c(0, 1), 
     xaxt = "n", 
     yaxt = "n")

obj1 <- seq1

obj2 <- seq2
# Calculate space available for sequences and spacing between them
available_space <- xlim - 5 - 5 - gap_size  # 5 spaces on each side, minus gap

# Calculate the space needed for each letter in each segment
space_per_letter <- available_space / (length(obj1) + length(obj2)) 

# Calculate the starting position for each segment
start_1 <- 5  # 5 spaces to the left
start_2 <- start_1 + length(obj1) * space_per_letter + gap_size  # Add gap between

# Create x-coordinates for each segment
x_coords_1 <- seq(start_1, start_1 + (length(obj1) - 1) * space_per_letter, length.out = length(obj1))
x_coords_2 <- seq(start_2, start_2 + (length(obj2) - 1) * space_per_letter, length.out = length(obj2))

# Plot the text
text(x = x_coords_1, y = rep(1, length(obj1)), labels = strsplit(as.character(obj1), "")[[1]])
text(x = x_coords_2, y = rep(1, length(obj2)), labels = strsplit(as.character(obj2), "")[[1]])
}

plot_sequence_full(gap_size = 10,seq1 = obj1,seq2 = obj2,xlim = 100)


```

Ok this worked so we want to also add in the complementary strands for these as well. And the dots. 

```{r}
plot_sequence_full <- function(gap_size=20,seq1,seq2,xlim=100,seperation_width=0.1,forward_primer=primer1,reverse_primer=primer2,max.miss = 6,target=NULL,plot_elongation=F){

  # get some basic plotting windows open
par(mar=c(1,1,1,1))
plot(x=1, 
     type = "n", 
     xlab = "", 
     ylab = "", 
     xlim = c(0,xlim), 
     ylim = c(0, 1.1), 
     xaxt = "n", 
     yaxt = "n")


# define your sequences and the reverse comps
obj1 <- seq1
comp_obj1 <- complement(seq1) # computes the complement
obj2 <- seq2
comp_obj2 <- complement(seq2) # computes the complement


# Forward Primer:
forward_p <- DNAString(forward_primer)
```

```{r}
# Load the functions:
# matching
get_primer_matches <- function(target=target,forward=primer1,reverse=primer2,max.miss=5){
  
# Convert the strings to DNAStrings()
  
target <- DNAString(target)
forward <- DNAString(forward)
reverse <- DNAString(reverse)

#get the max mismatch value
max.miss=max.miss

# find the primer 1 matches:  
p1_match <- Biostrings::matchPattern(pattern = forward,subject = target,max.mismatch = max.miss)
# test if the match length is 0
if (length(p1_match@ranges@width)==0){
  # primer1
  rcomp_primer1 <- reverseComplement(forward)
  rcomp_primer1
  best_match_p1 <- p1_match
  
#   print("The forward primer needed to be reverse complemented to be found in your target")
# p1_rcomp_match <- Biostrings::matchPattern(pattern = reverseComplement((forward)),subject = target,max.mismatch = max.miss)
# print(p1_rcomp_match)
# print(rcomp_primer1)
  print("The forward primer was not found in your sequence. Check to make sure the primer matches or adjust the max.miss value")
} else {
  # if the match is not 0 then report the match
  print("The forward primer matches as is see below....")
  print(p1_match)
  best_match_p1 <- p1_match
}


# find the primer 2 matches
p2_match <- Biostrings::matchPattern(pattern = reverse,subject = target,max.mismatch = max.miss)

# check if the match is there
if (length(p2_match@ranges@width)==0){
  # primer2
  rcomp_primer2 <- reverseComplement(reverse)
  rcomp_primer2
  print("The reverse primer needed to be reverse complemented to be found in your target")
p2_rcomp_match <- Biostrings::matchPattern(pattern = reverseComplement((reverse)),subject = target,max.mismatch = max.miss)
print(p2_rcomp_match)
best_match_p2 <- p2_rcomp_match
} else {
  print("The reverse primer matches as is see below....")
  print(p2_match)
  best_match_p2 <- p2_match
}
# Return the matches in a list
  return(list(p1_match = best_match_p1, p2_match = best_match_p2))
}
```
